newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordanian soldier kills seven Israeli schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian soldier kills seven Israeli schoolgirls.

text.p: A Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls and wounded six while the children were on a field trip to the Israeli-Jordanian border on Thursday, officials said.
Israeli rescuers said they held the bodies of two girls. A hospital official in Jordan said five more Israelis had arrived dead at a hospital in northern Jordan.
"It looks like they were all schoolgirls who were on a tourist bus," the Jordanian official said. "Five of them were dead on arrival at the hospital."
The girls, aged 12 and 13, were on a school outing.
Witnesses said a bus had dropped them off in a farm area which Israel leases from Jordan under a 1994 peace deal.

A girl named Oranit, who was shot in the hand, told army radio: "We walked around and I heard shots...It was close...I turned around and saw a soldier taking a magazine from his rifle and firing and we ran to the hill...He shot me in the hand."
Other Jordanian soldiers overpowered the gunman.
Israeli radio stations said leaders of both countries were in contact.

"This was a wicked attack that brought about a terrible tragedy," Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told reporters. "We expect the Jordanian government to act to the full extent of the law on this matter."
Six Israelis were being treated for wounds, two of them at a Jordanian hospital in Shuna. Officials said Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti would fly by helicopter to the scene.

"We've had contacts with Jordan aimed at bringing back the wounded or the bodies to Israel as soon as possible. An Israeli helicopter will head to Jordan soon," ministry spokesman Danny Shek told Reuters.
Israelis and Palestinians had feared an outbreak of violence following the Israeli government's decision to forge ahead with a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Another witness said: "There is a huge great panic. Many, many security forces have arrived." Helicopters hovered overhead.
Jordan and Israel signed a treaty in October 1994 and their border has been quiet for years.

But Jordan's King Hussein warned Israel this week it was pushing the Middle East into crisis by dictating terms of its withdrawal from West Bank areas and building Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem.
He also warned of a "very strong chance of violence" if Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushed ahead with plans for a Jewish settlement on the outskirts of Arab East Jerusalem.
"There is a problem with the best of our neighbours," Israeli Education Minister Zevulun Hammer told army radio.

"Ninety percent of the Knesset voted for this peace and look what happens just for the heck of it. No one provoked here. There was no provocation," said Hammer, of the right-wing National Religious Party.
"Perhaps the conclusion is that the king must hold his tongue so that a soldier doesn't take his words to mean more than he intended," he said.
